# Story 10.1: Unit tests for column widths fitting content (Universe Ex-Date)

Status: done

## Story

As a developer,
I want a red-phase unit-test scaffold asserting that the Universe table's Ex-Date column is wide enough to display its editable date input without truncation,
So that Story 10.2 has a defined, executable contract to make pass when it widens the column.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A unit test asserts the `ex_date` column definition in `apps/dms-material/src/app/global/global-universe/global-universe.columns.ts` declares a width sufficient for an editable date input — specifically that its `width` is at least 200px (the current value of 175 truncates the input).
2. A unit test renders the Universe table and asserts the Ex-Date column's `<mat-header-cell>` / `<mat-cell>` computed width equals the declared column width (i.e. the binding `[style.width.px]="column.width ?? DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTH"` is honored), so a widened definition actually widens the rendered cell.
3. All new assertions in this story are marked `.skip()` (`it.skip`) in code so CI stays green while the width is still 175; every pre-existing test remains unskipped and green.

## Tasks / Subtasks

- [x] Task 1: Add red-phase tests for the Ex-Date column width (AC: #1, #2)
  - [x] 1.1 In `apps/dms-material/src/app/global/global-universe/global-universe.component.spec.ts` (or a sibling spec), import the `global-universe.columns.ts` definitions and assert the `ex_date` entry's `width >= 200`.
  - [x] 1.2 Add a render test asserting the Ex-Date `<mat-cell>`/`<mat-header-cell>` computed width matches the declared column width (binding honored).
- [x] Task 2: Mark all new tests `.skip()` so CI stays green (AC: #3)
  - [x] 2.1 Prefix each new `it(...)` with `.skip` and add a comment noting Story 10.2 removes the skips, confirms red, then implements until green.

## Dev Notes

- Red-phase TDD convention: this story writes failing tests marked `.skip()` in code so CI stays green; Story 10.2's FIRST task is to remove those skips, confirm they fail (red), then implement until green.
- **Current state verified on disk:** `apps/dms-material/src/app/global/global-universe/global-universe.columns.ts` declares `{ field: 'ex_date', header: 'Ex-Date', type: 'date', ..., width: 175 }`. The Ex-Date cell is an editable date input (`<dms-editable-date-cell>` / mat-form-field) in the universe custom `#cellTemplate`; at 175px the input is truncated.
- **Why a width assertion on the definition:** the rendered width is driven entirely by the column's `width` field via `[style.width.px]="column.width ?? DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTH"` in base-table, so asserting the declared value (plus one binding-honored render check) is the precise, deterministic contract — no pixel-scraping of a live input.
- **Scope:** the Epic prose lists Universe Ex-Date as the known truncation site ("There may be other places I miss"). This story targets that confirmed case; Story 10.2 notes how to extend if more narrow columns surface during review.

### Project Structure Notes

- Add: new `it` blocks in the global-universe spec (or a sibling spec). No production code changes in this story.
- No conflict: pure test scaffold; it does not modify the column definitions or templates.
